title: Blood–brain barrier opening with focused ultrasound reduces neuromelanin in a non-human primate model
title_zh: 聚焦超声诱导血脑屏障开启可降低非人灵长类动物模型中的神经黑素
abstract: Abstract Age-related accumulation of neuromelanin (NM) has been implicated in the intrinsic vulnerability of catecholaminergic neurons in Parkinson’s disease. Postmortem studies in Parkinson’s disease patients have revealed elevated intracellular and extracellular NM in the substantia nigra pars compacta, whereas experimental enhancement of NM synthesis in animal models disrupts neuronal homeostasis and accelerates neurodegeneration. Low-intensity focused ultrasound combined with microbubbles (LIFU-MB) induces focal opening of the blood–brain barrier. It has been shown to influence protein aggregation and modulate pigment-related processes, thereby raising the possibility that it may also impact NM dynamics in the brain. Here, we investigated the possibility that repeated LIFU-MB–mediated blood–brain barrier opening could modify NM accumulation in a non-human primate model that overexpresses human tyrosinase, leading to elevated NM accumulation in the substantia nigra pars compacta. Comprehensive characterization revealed that these animals exhibit several features compatible with early pathological changes in Parkinson’s disease including extracellular NM release, increased iron accumulation, nigral inflammatory changes, and intracellular inclusion formation. Importantly, these alterations occur in the absence of substantial dopaminergic cell loss and behavioral deficits. LIFU-MB–treated animals showed a marked reduction in both intracellular and extracellular NM, accompanied by a trend toward decreased free ferric iron. These results indicate that early, non-invasive LIFU-MB intervention can counteract mechanisms linked to excessive NM accumulation. Moreover, this approach provides a translational framework to explore the broader feasibility of reducing intracellular pigments and pathological aggregates in the brain. Given its clinical safety, capacity to reach deep brain structures, and non-invasive nature, LIFU-MB warrants further investigation as a possible therapeutic approach in Parkinson´s disease and other neurodegenerative disorders.
abstract_zh: 摘要：与年龄相关的神经黑素（NM）积累已被认为与帕金森病中儿茶酚胺能神经元的内在易感性相关。帕金森病患者的尸检研究显示黑质致密部细胞内外NM升高，而在动物模型中实验性增强NM合成会破坏神经元稳态并加速神经退行。低强度聚焦超声结合微泡（LIFU‑MB）可诱导血脑屏障局部开启。已有研究表明其可影响蛋白聚集并调节色素相关过程，从而提出其可能影响脑内NM动力学。本文探讨了在过表达人类酪氨酸酶、导致黑质致密部NM积累升高的非人灵长类动物模型中，重复LIFU‑MB介导的血脑屏障开启是否能改变NM积累。全面表征显示，这些动物表现出与帕金森病早期病理变化相符的多种特征，包括细胞外NM释放、铁积聚增加、黑质炎症改变和细胞内包涵体形成。值得注意的是，这些改变发生在没有显著多巴胺能细胞丢失和行为缺陷的情况下。LIFU‑MB处理组动物的细胞内外NM显著减少，并伴随自由铁离子下降的趋势。这些结果表明，早期非侵入性LIFU‑MB干预可抵消与过度NM积累相关的机制。此外，该方法为探索降低脑内细胞色素和病理聚集体的更广泛可行性提供了转化框架。鉴于其临床安全性、可达深脑结构的能力以及非侵入性特征，LIFU‑MB值得进一步研究，作为帕金森病及其他神经退行性疾病的潜在治疗手段。
